boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Wilson's Creek record (August 10, 1861) in Operations to Control Missouri [June-October 1861]. The August 2 skirmish at Dug Springs, the approach marches and the retreat to Rolla are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the Army of the West and the Missouri State Guard with McCulloch's brigade, with no figures; the live field reads zero. Sturgis says 3,700 men attacked an enemy numbering 23,000 and that over 20,000 were still in front at Lyon's death. Snead gives Sigel's column about twelve hundred and Lyon's about four thousand two hundred; the Union 3,500 who went into action on Bloody Hill against Price's 4,200 there; Price's first line over thirty-one hundred against Lyon's front of nearly nineteen hundred; McIntosh's thousand in the cornfield; and Pearce's idle brigade of more than 1,700. Snead also calls Lyon's army six or seven thousand and the Confederate force twice as great.
claims.rationale: Column, engaged, sector and whole-army figures of different populations and moments, from an interested Union report and a Confederate participant history. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Major General Sterling Price and Brigadier General Ben McCulloch, Brigadier General Nathaniel Lyon and Samuel D. Sturgis as Major General; Sturgis signs his report as Major, First Cavalry. Snead says McCulloch accepted command of the combined armies and Price turned over the State Guard to him. Lyon was killed; Sturgis says Schofield reported to him for orders, and Snead that command devolved on Sturgis, who decided to retreat.
claims.rationale: Command roles from a participant history and an interested report; no automatic sole credit, and the frozen rank for Sturgis is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 2,330 (US 1,235; CS 1,095); the live field reads 1,781 (US 1,317; CS 464). Sturgis reports 1,235 killed, wounded and missing, matching the total of the return printed with his report, and guesses the enemy's at 3,000. Snead gives 1,317 Federal killed, wounded and missing and 1,230 Confederate killed and wounded, and 293 lost in Sigel's column.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The return's columns are garbled in OCR; only its printed total is cited.

open_questions: Fremont's, Lyon's August 9, Schofield's, Sigel's No. 13, Price's No. 19 and McCulloch's No. 21 reports, the subordinate reports and McClellan's indorsement on Sturgis's report remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Thomas L. Snead's The Fight for Missouri (Scribner, 1886) is a retrospective history by the Missouri State Guard's acting adjutant-general and Price's chief of staff, who says he was with the Governor at Booneville and Carthage; it quotes Sigel's, Schofield and Sturgis's and Price's reports and is not independent of them. Sturgis's August 20, 1861 report and the return of casualties printed with it are an interested Union account, the same author family as the Sturgis reports registered for Dandridge; Sturgis says he drew largely on Schofield's memoranda. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
